correctness.rationale: (P3) and (P4) give consequent reduction; identity and normality imply a unique principal-filter generator for each Boolean truth coordinate. P2 and MP force singleton self-fibers; P5 is equivalent by quantifying over all consequents to the strong-density inclusion for every D subset A. On three atoms only six singleton fibers and three pair fibers remain; two displayed implications are exhaustive. Direct evaluation of every axiom for all 4,096 candidate operations agrees with independently implemented strong density. The 64-case product formula gives 1,235, the S3 fixed counts are (1235,35,11), Burnside gives 227, and the restricted functional count is 283. Uniqueness forces intrinsic multivaluedness in the other 952; at most two atoms every free fiber is subset of a singleton. Checks extend no unjustified infinite inference.

value.rationale: Nondeterministic selection is a substantive semantic distinction in conditional logic, and the first Boolean carrier where it becomes unavoidable is a natural sharp boundary. The result completely enumerates all labelled and symmetry-quotiented eight-element normal MP preconditionals and separates deterministic selection from genuine set-valued behavior. This is not the previously known general representation theorem, nor an arbitrary uninterpreted numerical slice; the proof gives a structural uniform finite selector normal form and a 64-term exact derivation.
